tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman?

options.A: She advocates animal protection.
options.B: She sells a special kind of coffee.
options.C: She is going to start a cafe chain.
options.D: She is the owner of a special cafe.

questions.cn: 关于这位女士，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.B: 她卖一种特别的咖啡。
optionsCn.C: 她打算开一家连锁咖啡馆。
optionsCn.D: 她是一家特色咖啡馆的老板。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about cafés in her city?

options.A: They bear a lot of similarities.
options.B: They are a profitable business sector.
options.C: They cater to different customers.
options.D: They help take care of customers' pets.

questions.cn: 关于她所在城市的咖啡馆，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 它们是很赚钱的商业领域。
optionsCn.C: 它们服务于不同的顾客。
optionsCn.D: 它们帮忙照看顾客的宠物。

questions.stem: How does the Parisian café guarantee that its rabbits pose no health threat?

options.A: By giving them regular cleaning and injections.
options.B: By selecting breeds that are tame and peaceful.
options.C: By placing them at a safe distance from customers.
options.D: By briefing customers on how to get along with them.

questions.cn: “巴黎人咖啡馆”如何确保其兔子不构成健康威胁？

optionsCn.A: 通过定期为它们清洁和注射疫苗。
optionsCn.B: 通过挑选温顺平和的品种。
optionsCn.C: 通过让它们与顾客保持安全距离。
optionsCn.D: 通过向顾客说明如何与它们相处。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about their customers?

options.A: They want to learn about rabbits.
options.B: They like to bring in their children.
options.C: They love the animals in her cafe.
options.D: They give her cafe favorite reviews.

questions.cn: 关于他们的顾客，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.B: 他们喜欢带孩子来。
optionsCn.C: 他们喜爱她咖啡馆里的动物。
optionsCn.D: 他们给她咖啡馆好评。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Tonight we have a special guest from a local establishment, the Parisian Café.
lines.cn: M：今晚我们请到了一位特别来宾，来自本地一家名为“巴黎人咖啡馆”的店铺。

lines.t: M: Welcome.
lines.cn: M：欢迎您。

lines.t: F: Hi, thanks for having me on your show.
lines.cn: F：你好，谢谢你们邀请我上节目。

lines.t: M: Thank you for joining us.
lines.cn: M：谢谢您来参加我们的节目。

lines.t: M: So please tell us, why did you decide to open a café?
lines.cn: M：那请告诉我们，您为什么决定开一家咖啡馆？

lines.t: F: Well, we saw the opportunity to offer something a little special and different from other establishments.
lines.cn: F：嗯，我们看到了一个机会，可以提供一些比其他店更特别、更与众不同的东西。

lines.t: F: Cafés certainly are a very competitive market sector.
lines.cn: F：咖啡馆确实是一个竞争非常激烈的市场领域。

lines.t: F: There are more than plenty in our city and we felt they are all rather similar to each other.
lines.cn: F：我们这座城市里的咖啡馆多得数不清，而我觉得它们彼此都相当相似。

lines.t: F: Wouldn't you agree?
lines.cn: F：您不觉得是这样吗？

lines.t: M: Certainly, yes.
lines.cn: M：的确如此。

lines.t: M: So how is your establishment any different?
lines.cn: M：那你们这家店有什么不同呢？

lines.t: F: Well, simply put, we have rabbits wandering freely around the place.
lines.cn: F：简单说，我们店里有许多兔子自由自在地到处跑。

lines.t: F: Our customers come in and enjoy their food and drinks, while little rabbits play about and brush against their legs.
lines.cn: F：顾客进来享用食物和饮品，小兔子就在旁边玩耍，蹭着他们的腿。

lines.t: F: There's no other place like it.
lines.cn: F：没有别的地方像这样。

lines.t: M: That's amazing.
lines.cn: M：太不可思议了。

lines.t: M: How did you come up with the idea?
lines.cn: M：您是怎么想到这个主意的？

lines.t: F: We saw other cafés with cats in them, so we thought, why not rabbits?
lines.cn: F：我们看到别的咖啡馆里养猫，于是就想，为什么不能是兔子呢？

lines.t: F: People love rabbits.
lines.cn: F：人们喜欢兔子。

lines.t: F: They are very cute animals.
lines.cn: F：它们是非常可爱的动物。

lines.t: M: But is it safe?
lines.cn: M：但这样安全吗？

lines.t: M: Do the rabbits ever bite people or do any customers ever hurt the rabbits?
lines.cn: M：兔子会咬人吗？或者有顾客伤害过兔子吗？

lines.t: F: It's perfectly safe for both the rabbits and our customers.
lines.cn: F：对兔子和顾客来说都完全安全。

lines.t: F: Rabbits are very peaceful and certainly do not bite.
lines.cn: F：兔子非常温顺，肯定不会咬人。

lines.t: F: Furthermore, our rabbits are regularly cleaned and have all received the required shots, so there is no health risk whatsoever.
lines.cn: F：此外，我们的兔子定期清洁，也都打了必需的疫苗，所以完全不存在健康风险。

lines.t: F: As for our customers, they are all animal lovers, so they would never try to hurt the rabbits.
lines.cn: F：至于我们的顾客，他们都是喜爱动物的人，绝不会去伤害兔子。

lines.t: F: Sometimes a young child may get over-excited and be a little too rough, but it's never a serious matter.
lines.cn: F：有时小孩子会过于兴奋、动作有点粗鲁，但从来不是什么严重的事。

lines.t: F: On the contrary, the Parisian café offers a great experience for children, a chance for them to learn about rabbits and how to take care of them.
lines.cn: F：恰恰相反，“巴黎人咖啡馆”为孩子提供了很棒的体验，让他们有机会了解兔子以及如何照顾它们。

lines.t: M: Well, it's certainly the first time I've heard of a café like that.
lines.cn: M：嗯，这样的咖啡馆我确实是第一次听说。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do the speakers say about the food their children like?

options.A: It contains too many additives.
options.B: It lacks the essential vitamins.
options.C: It can cause obesity.
options.D: It is mostly garbage.

questions.cn: 两位说话人怎么评价他们孩子喜欢的食物？

optionsCn.B: 它缺乏必需的维生素。
optionsCn.C: 它会导致肥胖。
optionsCn.D: 它多半是垃圾食品。

questions.stem: According to the speakers, what affects children's choice of food most?

options.A: Its fancy design.
options.B: TV commercials.
options.C: Its taste and texture.
options.D: Peer influence.

questions.cn: 根据说话人，最影响孩子食物选择的是什么？

optionsCn.B: 电视广告。
optionsCn.C: 它的味道和口感。
optionsCn.D: 同伴的影响。

questions.stem: What do the speakers believe big food corporations are doing?

options.A: Investing heavily in the production of sweet foods.
options.B: Marketing their products with ordinary ingredients.
options.C: Trying to trick children into buying their products.
options.D: Offering children more variables to choose from.

questions.cn: 两位说话人认为大型食品公司在做什么？

optionsCn.B: 用普通食材来推销产品。
optionsCn.C: 设法诱骗孩子购买他们的产品。
optionsCn.D: 给孩子提供更多可选择的品种。

questions.stem: What do we know about the speakers when they were children?

options.A: They hardly ate vegetables.
options.B: They seldom had junk food.
options.C: They favored chocolate-coated sweets.
options.D: They like the food advertised on TV.

questions.cn: 关于两位说话人小时候的情况，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.B: 他们很少吃垃圾食品。
optionsCn.C: 他们偏爱巧克力裹糖果。
optionsCn.D: 他们喜欢电视上做广告的食物。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: Hey there, how are you?
lines.cn: M：嗨，你好吗？

lines.t: F: Oh, hi.
lines.cn: F：哦，你好。

lines.t: F: I'm great, thanks.
lines.cn: F：我很好，谢谢。

lines.t: F: And you look great too.
lines.cn: F：你看起来也很好。

lines.t: M: Thank you.
lines.cn: M：谢谢。

lines.t: M: It's good to see you shopping at the organics section.
lines.cn: M：看到你在有机食品区购物，真不错。

lines.t: M: I see you've got lots of healthy stuff.
lines.cn: M：我看你买了很多健康食品。

lines.t: F: I wish I could buy more organic produce from here, but I find the kids don't like it.
lines.cn: F：我倒希望能多买些这里的有机农产品，可我发现孩子们不喜欢。

lines.t: F: I don't know about yours, but mine are all about junk food.
lines.cn: F：不知道你家的孩子怎么样，我家孩子就只爱垃圾食品。

lines.t: M: Oh, trust me, I know exactly how you feel.
lines.cn: M：哦，相信我，我完全明白你的感受。

lines.t: M: My children are the same.
lines.cn: M：我的孩子也一样。

lines.t: M: What is it with kids these days and all that junk food they eat?
lines.cn: M：现在的孩子到底怎么了，怎么吃那么多垃圾食品？

lines.t: F: I think it's all that advertising on TV.
lines.cn: F：我觉得都是电视上那些广告造成的。

lines.t: F: That's where they get it.
lines.cn: F：他们就是从那儿学来的。

lines.t: M: Yes, it must be.
lines.cn: M：是啊，一定是这样。

lines.t: M: My children see something on TV and they immediately want it.
lines.cn: M：我的孩子在电视上看到什么，马上就想买。

lines.t: M: It's like they don't realise it's just an advertisement.
lines.cn: M：他们好像根本意识不到那只是广告。

lines.t: F: Right.
lines.cn: F：没错。

lines.t: M: And practically everything that's advertised for children is unhealthy processed foods.
lines.cn: M：而且几乎所有针对儿童投放广告的都是不健康的加工食品。

lines.t: M: No surprise then, it becomes a battle for us parents to feed our children ordinary fruit and vegetables.
lines.cn: M：所以毫不奇怪，我们做父母的想让孩子吃普通的水果蔬菜，简直成了一场战斗。

lines.t: F: That's just the thing.
lines.cn: F：问题就在这里。

lines.t: F: One never sees ordinary ingredients being advertised on TV.
lines.cn: F：电视上从来不会给普通食材做广告。

lines.t: F: It's never a carrot or a peach.
lines.cn: F：从来不是胡萝卜或桃子。

lines.t: F: It's always some garbage like chocolate covered sweets.
lines.cn: F：总是些像巧克力裹糖果这样的垃圾食品。

lines.t: F: So unhealthy.
lines.cn: F：太不健康了。

lines.t: M: Exactly.
lines.cn: M：正是。

lines.t: M: And these big food corporations have so much money to spend on clever tactics designed to make young children want to buy their products.
lines.cn: M：而这些大型食品公司有大笔的钱，用来施展种种巧妙手段，让小孩子想买他们的产品。

lines.t: M: Children never stand a chance.
lines.cn: M：孩子们根本没有招架之力。

lines.t: M: It's really not fair.
lines.cn: M：这真的不公平。

lines.t: F: You are so right.
lines.cn: F：你说得太对了。

lines.t: F: When we were children, we barely had any junk food available and we turned out just fine.
lines.cn: F：我们小时候几乎没什么垃圾食品可吃，我们不也长得挺好。

lines.t: M: Yes, my parents don't understand any of it.
lines.cn: M：是啊，我父母对这些完全不理解。

lines.t: M: Both the TV commercials and the supermarkets are alien to them.
lines.cn: M：电视广告和超市对他们来说都很陌生。

lines.t: M: Their world was so different back when they were young.
lines.cn: M：他们年轻时的世界实在太不一样了。

lines.t: F: I don't know what will happen to the next generation.
lines.cn: F：我不知道下一代人会变成什么样。

lines.t: F: The world is going crazy.
lines.cn: F：这世界快疯了。

lines.t: M: You bet.
lines.cn: M：可不是嘛。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What can be found in the Valley of the Kings?

options.A: Stretches of farmland.
options.B: Typical Egyptian animal farms.
options.C: Tombs of ancient rulers.
options.D: Ruins left by devastating floods.

questions.cn: 在帝王谷能看到什么？

optionsCn.B: 典型的埃及畜牧场。
optionsCn.C: 古代统治者的陵墓。
optionsCn.D: 毁灭性洪水留下的废墟。

questions.stem: In what way is the Amazon different from other big rivers?

options.A: It provides habitats for more primitive tribes.
options.B: It is hardly associated with great civilizations.
options.C: It has not yet been fully explored and exploited.
options.D: It gathers water from many tropical rain forests.

questions.cn: 亚马孙河在哪方面与其他大河不同？

optionsCn.A: 它为更多原始部落提供栖息地。
optionsCn.B: 它几乎与伟大文明没有关联。
optionsCn.C: 它尚未被充分开发和利用。
optionsCn.D: 它汇聚了来自许多热带雨林的水。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the Amazon?

options.A: It carries about one fifth of the word' fresh water.
options.B: It has numerous human settlements along its banks.
options.C: It is second only to the Mississippi River in width.
options.D: It is as long as the Nile and the Yangtze combined.

questions.cn: 关于亚马孙河，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它承载着全球约五分之一的淡水。
optionsCn.B: 它的两岸有众多人类定居点。
optionsCn.C: 它的宽度仅次于密西西比河。
optionsCn.D: 它的长度等于尼罗河与长江之和。

lines.t: Passage one.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: The Nile, which begins in central Africa and flows over 4,100 miles north into the Mediterranean, hosted one of the world's great ancient civilizations along its shores.
lines.cn: 尼罗河发源于非洲中部，向北流淌 4100 多英里注入地中海，沿岸孕育了世界上最伟大的古代文明之一。

lines.t: Calm and peaceful for most of the year, the Nile used to flood annually, thereby creating, irrigating and carrying new topsoil to the nearby farmland on which ancient Egypt depended for livelihood.
lines.cn: 尼罗河一年中大部分时间平静温和，过去每年都会泛滥，从而形成、灌溉并把新的表土带到附近的农田，古埃及正是依靠这些农田为生。

lines.t: As a means of transportation, the river carried various vessels up and down its length.
lines.cn: 作为运输通道，这条河承载着各种船只在上下游往来。

lines.t: A journey through the unobstructed part of this waterway today would pass by the splendid Valley of the Kings, where the tombs of many of these ancient monarchs have stood for over 3,000 years.
lines.cn: 今天，沿这条水道畅通的一段航行，会经过壮观的帝王谷，那里许多古代君主的陵墓已矗立了三千多年。

lines.t: Great civilizations and intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon.
lines.cn: 伟大的文明和密集的定居点几乎与亚马孙河无关。

lines.t: Yet this 4,000-mile-long South American river carries about 20% of the world's fresh water, more than the Mississippi, Nile and Yangtze combined.
lines.cn: 然而这条长达 4000 英里的南美河流承载着全球约 20% 的淡水，比密西西比河、尼罗河和长江加起来还多。

lines.t: Other statistics are equally astonishing.
lines.cn: 其他数据同样令人震惊。

lines.t: The Amazon is so wide at some points that from its centre neither shore can be seen.
lines.cn: 亚马孙河有些地方宽得从河中央望去，两岸都看不见。

lines.t: Each second, the Amazon pours some 55 million gallons of water into the Atlantic.
lines.cn: 每秒，亚马孙河向大西洋注入约 5500 万加仑的水。

lines.t: There, at its mouth, stands one island larger than Switzerland.
lines.cn: 在其入海口处，有一座比瑞士还大的岛。

lines.t: Most important of all, the Amazon irrigates the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.
lines.cn: 最重要的是，亚马孙河灌溉着地球上最大的热带雨林。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker think is an inevitable truth?

options.A: Living a life in the fast lane leads to success.
options.B: We are always in a rush to do various things.
options.C: The search for tranquility has become a trend.
options.D: All of us actually yearn for a slow and calm life .

questions.cn: 讲话者认为什么是无法回避的事实？

optionsCn.B: 我们总是匆忙地去做各种事情。
optionsCn.C: 追求宁静已成为一种潮流。
optionsCn.D: 我们其实都渴望缓慢平静的生活。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about her life in Tokyo?

options.A: She had trouble balancing family and work.
options.B: She enjoyed the various social events.
options.C: She was accustomed to tight schedules.
options.D: She spent all her leisure time writing books.

questions.cn: 关于她在东京的生活，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 她难以平衡家庭和工作。
optionsCn.B: 她很享受各种社交活动。
optionsCn.C: 她习惯了紧凑的日程。
optionsCn.D: 她把所有闲暇时间都用来写书。

questions.stem: What made the speaker change her lifestyle?

options.A: The possibility of ruining her family.
options.B: Becoming aware of her declining health.
options.C: The fatigue from living a fast-paced life.
options.D: Reading a book about slowing down.

questions.cn: 是什么让讲话者改变了自己的生活方式？

optionsCn.B: 意识到自己的健康状况在下降。
optionsCn.C: 快节奏生活带来的疲惫。
optionsCn.D: 读了一本关于慢下来的书。

questions.stem: What happened after the speaker changed her lifestyle?

options.A: She started to follow the cultural norms.
options.B: She came to enjoy doing everyday tasks.
options.C: She learns to use more polite expressions.
options.D: She stopped using to-do lists and calendars.

questions.cn: 讲话者改变生活方式之后发生了什么？

optionsCn.B: 她开始享受做日常事务。
optionsCn.C: 她学会使用更礼貌的表达。
optionsCn.D: 她不再使用待办清单和日历。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: How often do you say to people, I'm busy or I haven't got time for that?
lines.cn: 你有多常对别人说“我很忙”或者“我没时间做那件事”？

lines.t: It's an inevitable truth that all of us live a life in the fast lane, even though we know that being busy is not always particularly healthy.
lines.cn: 一个无法回避的事实是：我们所有人都过着快节奏的生活，尽管我们知道忙碌并不总是那么有益健康。

lines.t: Growing up in New Zealand, everything was always calm and slow.
lines.cn: 我在新西兰长大，那里的一切总是平静而缓慢。

lines.t: People enjoyed the tranquility of a slower pace of life.
lines.cn: 人们享受着慢节奏生活带来的宁静。

lines.t: But after I moved to Tokyo and lived there for a number of years, I got used to having a pile of to-do lists, and my calendar always looked like a mess with loads of things to do written across it.
lines.cn: 但在我搬到东京住了几年之后，我习惯了拥有一堆待办清单，我的日历总是乱糟糟的，上面写满了要做的事。

lines.t: I found myself filling my time up with endless work meetings and social events, rushing along as busy as a bee.
lines.cn: 我发现自己把时间填满了没完没了的工作会议和社交活动，忙得像只蜜蜂一样奔波。

lines.t: Then, one day, I came across a book called In Praise of Slowness, and realised that being busy is not only detrimental, but also has the danger of turning life into an endless race.
lines.cn: 后来有一天，我读到一本叫《慢的礼赞》的书，才意识到忙碌不仅有损健康，还有把生活变成无休止竞赛的危险。

lines.t: So I started practising the various practical steps mentioned by the author in the book, and began to revolt against the very idea of being too busy.
lines.cn: 于是我开始实践作者在书中提到的各种可行步骤，并开始反抗“过于忙碌”这一观念本身。

lines.t: It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist, but I've become more aware of the importance of slowing down, and making sure that I enjoy the daily activities as I carry them out.
lines.cn: 这并不意味着我的待办清单不复存在，而是我更清楚地意识到放慢脚步的重要性，并确保在做日常事务时能享受其中。

lines.t: From now on, when someone asks you how your life is, try responding with words like exciting and fun, instead of the cultural norm that says busy.
lines.cn: 从今以后，当有人问你生活得怎么样时，试着用“精彩”“有意思”这样的词回答，而不是用社会惯例里那个“忙”字。

lines.t: See if you experience the tranquillity that follows.
lines.cn: 看看你会不会感受到随之而来的那份宁静。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What assumption about introduced species is challenged by a number of scientists?

options.A: They will root out native species altogether.
options.B: They contribute to a region's biodiversity.
options.C: They pose a threat to the local ecosystem.
options.D: They will crossbreed with native species.

questions.cn: 关于引进物种的什么假设受到不少科学家的质疑？

optionsCn.A: 它们会把本地物种彻底铲除。
optionsCn.B: 它们有助于一个地区的生物多样性。
optionsCn.C: 它们对当地生态系统构成威胁。
optionsCn.D: 它们会与本地物种杂交。

questions.stem: What does Dr. Michael Rosenzweig think of exotic and native species?

options.A: Their classifications are meaningful.
options.B: Their interactions are hard to define.
options.C: Their definitions are changeable.
options.D: Their distinctions are artificial.

questions.cn: 迈克尔·罗森茨韦格博士如何看待外来物种和本地物种？

optionsCn.A: 它们的分类是有意义的。
optionsCn.B: 它们之间的相互作用难以界定。
optionsCn.C: 它们的定义是可变的。
optionsCn.D: 它们之间的区分是人为的。

questions.stem: What does Professor Don Smith say about alien species?

options.A: Only a few of them cause problems to native species.
options.B: They may turn to benefit the local environment
options.C: Few of them can survive in their new habitats.
options.D: Only 10 percent of them can be naturalized.

questions.cn: 唐·史密斯教授关于外来物种说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 其中只有少数会给本地物种造成问题。
optionsCn.B: 它们可能会转而有利于当地环境。
optionsCn.C: 它们中很少有能在新栖息地存活的。
optionsCn.D: 其中只有 10% 能够归化。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Governments, private groups and individuals spend billions of dollars a year trying to root out non-native organisms that are considered dangerous to ecosystems, and to prevent the introduction of new intruders.
lines.cn: 政府、私人团体和个人每年花费数十亿美元，试图铲除被认为对生态系统有害的外来生物，并阻止新入侵者的引入。

lines.t: But a number of scientists question the assumption that the presence of alien species can never be acceptable in a natural ecosystem.
lines.cn: 但不少科学家质疑这样一个假设：外来物种出现在自然生态系统中永远不可接受。

lines.t: They say that portraying introduced species as inherently bad is an unscientific approach.
lines.cn: 他们说，把引进物种一概描绘成本质上有害，是不科学的做法。

lines.t: Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial, said Dr.
lines.cn: 把外来物种与本地物种区分开来是人为的，

lines.t: Michael Rosenzweig, a professor of evolutionary biology at the University of Arizona.
lines.cn: 亚利桑那大学进化生物学教授迈克尔·罗森茨韦格博士说。

lines.t: Because they depend on picking a date and calling the plants and animals that show up after that date exotic.
lines.cn: 因为这取决于人为选定一个日期，然后把在该日期之后出现的动植物都称作外来的。

lines.t: Ecosystems free of species defined as exotic are, by default, considered the most natural.
lines.cn: 没有所谓外来物种的生态系统，默认就被认为是最自然的。

lines.t: You can't roll back the clock and remove all exotics or fix habitats, Dr.
lines.cn: 你无法让时钟倒转，把所有外来物种清除掉，或把栖息地修复如初，

lines.t: Rosenzweig said.
lines.cn: 罗森茨韦格博士说。

lines.t: Both native and exotic species can become invasive, and so they all have to be monitored and controlled when they begin to get out of hand.
lines.cn: 本地物种和外来物种都可能变成入侵物种，所以当它们开始失控时，都必须受到监测和控制。

lines.t: At its core, the debate is about how to manage the world's remaining natural ecosystems and about how and how much to restore other habitats.
lines.cn: 这场争论的核心是：如何管理世界上尚存的自然生态系统，以及如何、以多大力度修复其他栖息地。

lines.t: Species that invade a territory can harm ecosystems, agriculture and human health.
lines.cn: 入侵某一地域的物种会损害生态系统、农业和人类健康。

lines.t: They can threaten some native species or even destroy and replace others.
lines.cn: 它们可能威胁某些本地物种，甚至消灭并取代另一些物种。

lines.t: Next to habitat loss, these invasive species represent the greatest threat to biodiversity worldwide, many ecologists say.
lines.cn: 许多生态学家说，除栖息地丧失之外，这些入侵物种是全球生物多样性面临的最大威胁。

lines.t: Ecologists generally define an alien species as one that people accidentally or deliberately carried to its new location.
lines.cn: 生态学家通常把外来物种定义为：由人们无意或有意带到新地点的物种。

lines.t: Across the American continents, exotic species are those introduced after the first European contact.
lines.cn: 在整个美洲大陆，外来物种指的是欧洲人首次到达之后被引入的物种。

lines.t: That date, rounded off to 1500 AD, represents what ecologists consider to have been a major shift in the spread of species, including crops and livestock, as they began to migrate with humans from continent to continent.
lines.cn: 这个日期被大致定为公元 1500 年，它代表着生态学家所认为的物种传播上的重大转折，包括农作物和牲畜开始随人类从一个大陆迁移到另一个大陆。

lines.t: Only a small percentage of alien species cause problems in their new habitats, said Don Smith, professor of ecology and evolutionary biology at the University of Tennessee.
lines.cn: 田纳西大学生态学与进化生物学教授唐·史密斯说，只有一小部分外来物种会在新栖息地造成问题。

lines.t: Of the 7,000 alien species in the United States, out of a total of 150 ,000 species, only about 10% are invasive, he pointed out.
lines.cn: 他指出，在美国总共 15 万个物种中，7000 个外来物种里只有约 10% 是入侵物种。

lines.t: The other 90% have fit into their environments and are considered naturalized.
lines.cn: 其余 90% 已融入当地环境，被视为归化物种。

lines.t: Yet appearances can deceive, ecologists caution, and many of these exotics may be considered acceptable only because no one has documented their harmful effects.
lines.cn: 不过生态学家提醒说，表象可能骗人，这些外来物种中有许多之所以被认为可以接受，只是因为还没有人记录下它们的有害影响。

lines.t: What is more, non-native species can appear harmless for decades, then turn invasive.
lines.cn: 更何况，非本地物种可能几十年都显得无害，之后却变成入侵物种。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Good morning ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the third in our series of business seminars in the programme Doing Business Abroad.
lines.cn: 女士们、先生们，早上好，欢迎参加“海外经商”系列商务讲座的第三讲。

lines.t: Today we are going to look at intercultural awareness, that is, the fact that not everyone is British, not everyone speaks English, and not everyone does business in a British way.
lines.cn: 今天我们要谈谈跨文化意识，也就是说：并非人人都是英国人，并非人人都会说英语，也并非人人都按英国的方式做生意。

lines.t: And why should they?
lines.cn: 而他们又何必如此呢？

lines.t: If overseas business people are selling to us, then they will make every effort to speak English and to respect our traditions and methods.
lines.cn: 如果海外商人要向我们销售产品，他们会尽力说英语，尊重我们的传统和方式。

lines.t: It is only polite for us to do the same when we visit them.
lines.cn: 我们去拜访他们时，也同样这么做才算礼貌。

lines.t: It is not only polite, it is essential if we want to sell British products overseas.
lines.cn: 这不仅关乎礼貌，若想把英国产品卖到海外，这也是必不可少的。

lines.t: First, a short quiz.
lines.cn: 首先，做个小测验。

lines.t: Let's see how interculturally aware you are.
lines.cn: 看看你们的跨文化意识有多强。

lines.t: Where must you not drink alcohol on the 1st and 7th of every month?
lines.cn: 在哪个国家，每月 1 日和 7 日不能喝酒？

lines.t: OK, everyone had a chance to make some notes?
lines.cn: 好，大家都记下答案了吗？

lines.t: Right, here are the answers.
lines.cn: 好，答案来了。

lines.t: Although I am sure that the information could equally well apply to countries other than those I have chosen.
lines.cn: 尽管我相信这些信息同样适用于我选的那些国家之外的其他国家。

lines.t: So, number 1.
lines.cn: 那么，第一题。

lines.t: You must not drink alcohol on the 1st and 7th of the month in India.
lines.cn: 在印度，每月 1 日和 7 日不能喝酒。

lines.t: In international hotels you may find it served, but if you are having a meal with an Indian colleague, remember to avoid asking for a beer if your arrival coincides with one of those dates.
lines.cn: 在国际酒店里你可能会看到酒水供应，但如果你和印度同事一起吃饭，而你的到访恰逢这两个日子之一，记得不要点啤酒。

lines.t: In Arab countries, the politeness and generosity of the people is without parallel.
lines.cn: 在阿拉伯国家，人们的礼貌与慷慨无与伦比。

lines.t: If you admire your colleague's beautiful golden bowls, you may well find yourself being presented with them as a present.
lines.cn: 如果你赞赏同事那只漂亮的金碗，很可能就会收到它作为礼物。

lines.t: This is not a cheap way to do your shopping, however, as your host will quite correctly expect you to respond by presenting him with a gift of equal worth and beauty.
lines.cn: 不过这可不是省钱的购物方式，因为你的主人理所当然会期待你回赠一份价值与精美程度相当的礼物。

lines.t: In Thailand, clicking the fingers, clapping your hands or just shouting waiter will embarrass your hosts, fellow diners, the waiter himself and, most of all, you.
lines.cn: 在泰国，打响指、拍手或直接大喊“服务生”，会让主人、同桌客人、服务生本人尴尬，最尴尬的还是你自己。

lines.t: Place your palm downward and make an inconspicuous waving gesture which will produce instant and satisfying results.
lines.cn: 把手掌朝下，做一个不显眼的招手动作，效果立刻就会令人满意。

lines.t: And finally, in Spain, some businesses maintain the pattern of working until about 2 o'clock and then returning to the office from 5 .
lines.cn: 最后，在西班牙，一些企业保持着这样一种作息：工作到下午两点左右，然后从下午 5

lines.t: 30 to 8, 9 or 10 in the evening.
lines.cn: 点半到晚上 8 点、9 点或 10 点再回办公室。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Shortly after he took over the Reader's Digest Association in 1984, George Gruen unlocked the company's boardroom and announced that the room was now open to the employees.
lines.cn: 1984 年接管《读者文摘》公司后不久，乔治·格鲁恩打开了公司董事会议室的门，宣布这个房间现在向员工开放。

lines.t: It was a symbolic act, indicating that under Gruen's leadership, Reader's Digest was going to be different.
lines.cn: 这是一个象征性的举动，表明在格鲁恩的领导下，《读者文摘》将变得不同。

lines.t: True to his word, Gruen has shaken up the culture here.
lines.cn: 格鲁恩说到做到，彻底撼动了这里的企业文化。

lines.t: To get an idea of the culture we're talking about, consider the boardroom Gruen opened up.
lines.cn: 想了解我们所说的这种文化，就看看格鲁恩开放的那间董事会议室。

lines.t: It has artworks that any museum in the world would want to collect, paintings by many world-famous artists like Monet and Picasso.
lines.cn: 里面有世界上任何博物馆都想要收藏的艺术品，包括莫奈、毕加索等众多世界著名画家的画作。

lines.t: Its headquarters houses some 3,000 works of art.
lines.cn: 它的总部收藏着约 3000 件艺术品。

lines.t: The main building is topped with a Georgian tower with four sculptures of the mythical winged horse, the magazine's corporate logo.
lines.cn: 主楼顶部是乔治亚风格的塔楼，上面立着四个神话中飞马的雕像，那是这本杂志的企业标志。

lines.t: It sits on 127 acres of well-trimmed lawns.
lines.cn: 它坐落在一片修剪整齐、占地 127 英亩的草坪上。

lines.t: The editor's office used to be occupied by founder DeWitt Wallace, who, along with his wife, Leila Aitchison Wallace, launched Reader's Digest in 1922 with condensed articles from other publications.
lines.cn: 主编办公室曾由创始人德威特·华莱士使用，他和妻子莱拉·艾奇逊·华莱士于 1922 年创办《读者文摘》，专门刊登其他出版物的文章节选。

lines.t: It has become the world's most widely read magazine, selling 28 million copies each month in 17 languages and 41 different editions.
lines.cn: 它已成为世界上读者最多的杂志，每月以 17 种语言、41 个不同版本售出 2800 万册。

lines.t: The Wallaces, both children of church ministers, had a clearly defined formula for their little magazine, as Reader's Digest was originally subtitled.
lines.cn: 华莱士夫妇都是牧师的孩子，他们为这本小杂志定下了一套明确的公式——《读者文摘》最初的副标题就是“小杂志”。

lines.t: Articles were to be short, readable, and uplifting.
lines.cn: 文章要短小、易读、令人振奋。

lines.t: Subjects were picked to inspire or entertain.
lines.cn: 选题以鼓舞人心或提供娱乐为标准。

lines.t: The Wallaces didn't accept advertising in the U .
lines.cn: 华莱士夫妇的美国版

lines.t: S.
lines.cn: 直到 1955 年才

lines.t: edition until 1955, and even then they didn't allow any ads for cigarettes, liquor, or drugs.
lines.cn: 接受广告；即便到那时，他们也不允许任何香烟、烈酒或药品的广告。

lines.t: The Wallaces also had a clear sense of the kind of workplace they wanted.
lines.cn: 华莱士夫妇对自己想要什么样的工作场所也有清晰的设想。

lines.t: It started as a mom-and-pop operation, and the childless Wallaces always considered employees to be part of their family.
lines.cn: 公司起初只是夫妻小店式的经营，没有子女的华莱士夫妇一直把员工视为自己家庭的一部分。

lines.t: Employees still tell stories of how the Wallaces would take care of employees who had met with misfortunes, and they showered their employees with unusual benefits, like a turkey at Thanksgiving and Fridays off in May.
lines.cn: 员工们至今还在讲华莱士夫妇如何照顾遭遇不幸的员工，他们给员工提供了种种不同寻常的福利，比如感恩节送火鸡、五月里周五放假。

lines.t: This cozy workplace no longer exists here.
lines.cn: 这种温馨的工作环境在这里已不复存在。

lines.t: The Wallaces both died in their 90s in the early 1980s.
lines.cn: 华莱士夫妇都在 20 世纪 80 年代初以九十多岁高龄去世。

lines.t: George Gruen, a former ad salesman who joined Reader's Digest in 1960, has his eye focused on the bottom line.
lines.cn: 1960 年加入《读者文摘》的前广告销售员乔治·格鲁恩，眼睛只盯着利润。

lines.t: In a few short years, he turned the magazine on its head.
lines.cn: 短短几年里，他把这本杂志彻底翻了个个儿。

lines.t: He laid off several hundred workers.
lines.cn: 他裁掉了几百名员工。

lines.t: Especially hard-hit were the blue and pink-collar departments, such as subscription fulfillment.
lines.cn: 受影响尤其严重的是蓝领和粉领部门，比如订阅业务部门。
